title: MessagePack
subtitle: Compact binary serialisation on the agent runtime's message bus and the broker's internal entries.

stats.label: fixed fields in every write message
encodings, each chosen for its path

lede: In FAFO Core and Function Forge I wanted hundreds of workers to write results without any of them holding a database connection, so functions never write to PostgreSQL directly. A producer client encodes each write as a flat MessagePack message and appends it fire-and-forget to a Redis stream. A single governed write service then owns the write, one path from many producers into the database. I chose MessagePack because producers needed a compact, self-describing encoding that the writer could route without decoding the whole message. On a hot path I prefer a flat, fixed field set: the writer reads where a message goes with no database query and no schema lookup. The flat contract also taught me a lesson.
quote: A wire contract that matters has to be checked where it is consumed.
evidence: Write-path design: producers append flat MessagePack messages with 16 fixed fields to a Redis stream, so no worker holds a database connection.
Data contract enforcement: a convention-only contract left one producer's messages stranded, so contracts are now checked where they are consumed.
Serialisation design: MessagePack, canonical CBOR and bincode each chosen for what its path needs.
author: Corey James
